name: Command & Control Frameworks
tagline: C2 / post-exploitation frameworks, communication profiles, payload & beacon kits, and infrastructure helpers — for authorized adversary simulation, C2-traffic detection testing, and lab post-exploitation.

tools.name: Sliver
tools.desc: Open-source cross-platform adversary-emulation framework (BishopFox); Go implants are dynamically compiled with per-binary encryption keys and support C2 over mTLS, WireGuard, HTTP(S), and DNS.
tools.when: Your default lab/red-team C2 when you want a framework blue teams can profile exhaustively without commercial licensing.

tools.name: Mythic
tools.desc: Collaborative, Docker-based post-exploitation platform whose core ships no agents; you install agent payload types (Apollo/.NET, Athena/Rust, and others) and C2 profiles as separate containers via mythic-cli and the Mythic scripting API.
tools.when: Long-running lab engagements needing a pluggable, community-vetted agent ecosystem, cross-team collaboration, and GraphQL/automation hooks for red-team reporting.

tools.name: Empire
tools.desc: BC-Security's maintained fork of PowerShell Empire: PowerShell, Python, and C# agents with HTTP, HTTPS, HTTP(S)-SMB, and WebSocket listeners plus a REST API that Starkiller builds on.
tools.when: Classic PowerShell-heavy post-exploitation tradecraft whose agent traffic pairs naturally with the Starkiller UI; still the reference for Empire-style stager patterns.

tools.name: Havoc
tools.desc: Modern malleable post-exploitation framework pairing a Qt client with a Go teamserver; the Demon agent speaks AES-encrypted HTTP(S)/SMB and uses indirect syscalls. Maintenance stopped — repo archived Feb 2026 — yet it stays a heavily studied, MITRE-tracked (S1229) traffic class.
tools.when: Lab and detection research against a well-documented post-exploitation stack (tunnel, AMSI/ETW patching, BOF/COFF loading) whose artifacts most EDRs now fingerprint.

tools.name: Merlin
tools.desc: Go-based post-exploitation server/agent pair communicating over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, h2c, and HTTP/3 (QUIC) — a practical model for non-TLS and modern protocol beaconing.
tools.when: Lab tests of HTTP/2 and QUIC transport detection, since most defensive tuning focuses on plain HTTPS beacon patterns.

tools.name: Covenant
tools.desc: Collaborative .NET C2 with a browser UI whose Grunt implants are dynamically compiled C# — the canonical worked example of .NET post-exploitation patterns (in-memory loading, AMSI/ETW patching, SMB P2P). Effectively unmaintained since ~2021 (last push 2024); now a lab/museum reference and signature-rich detection target.
tools.when: Studying .NET post-exploitation design and beating on well-known signatures in the lab; treat it as a legacy framework, not for live operations.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/cobbr/Covenant && cd Covenant/Covenant && dotnet build -c Release

tools.name: Villain
tools.desc: High-level stage 0/1 C2 handler for many reverse-TCP and HoaxShell (HTTPS) shells, shipped with Windows/Linux payload templates, fileless scripting, and cross-instance session sharing.
tools.when: Quick-sided Kali lab work that needs concurrent shell handling and payload-template experimentation without standing up a full framework.

tools.name: PoshC2
tools.desc: Python-based C2 with PowerShell and C# tasking, impacket-driven implant generation, and in-memory staging — a lightweight, well-documented write-up of multi-listener C2 architecture.
tools.when: A small, quick-to-stand-up C2 for teaching listener/server concepts or comparing stager patterns against a mainstream framework.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.desc: Rapid7's framework in its C2 role: multi/handler listeners, staged Meterpreter/Python payloads, session and pivot management, plus the post-exploitation and exploit modules that hash-complete the ecosystem behind msfvenom.
tools.when: A lab C2/orchestrator when you want built-in listeners plus post-exploitation modules in one place; the baseline everyone's detection stack is tuned to.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.desc: Commercial threat-emulation platform (Fortra) and the de-facto reference C2; Malleable C2 profiles reshape HTTP(S)/DNS beacon traffic into the traffic shapes blue teams tune their detections around. Vetted licensing only: new licenses roughly $3.5k–$10k/user/yr, with cracked builds aggressively taken down.
tools.when: When you are an authorized red team that can buy it, or to study the beacon patterns that dominate C2 detection research.

tools.name: Starkiller
tools.desc: A community-built Electron UI over Empire's REST API: manage listeners, agents, modules, and credentials visually instead of via the cli client.
tools.when: Pair with Empire when a GUI makes listener/agent management and lab demos easier to follow.

tools.name: C2concealer
tools.desc: Red Siege's generator that crafts random, unique Malleable C2 profiles for Cobalt Strike and validates them by checking profile syntax against a reference server.
tools.when: Generate a fresh, randomized C2 profile per lab campaign so beacon traffic doesn't match known profile hashes.

tools.name: Malleable-C2-Randomizer
tools.desc: BluScreenofJeff's framework of profile-randomization scripts that shuffle URI paths, user-agents, and headers to defeat simple static signature matching.
tools.when: Lab experiments in yanking profile parts around and measuring how detection shifts between variants.

tools.name: pyMalleableC2
tools.desc: byt3bl33d3r's Python library that reads and rewrites Malleable C2 profile files programmatically, letting scripts tweak jitter, URIs, and headers in bulk.
tools.when: Deterministic profile transformation in scripts rather than hand-editing .profile files.

tools.name: rsmudge malleable-c2-profiles
tools.desc: Raphael Mudge's reference profile collection shipped alongside Cobalt Strike docs: the canonical .profile examples (amazon, gmail, outlook, etc.) that blue teams dissect to learn beacon shaping.
tools.when: Start from maintained, syntax-correct profiles when learning the Malleable C2 language and its transforms.

tools.name: threatexpress malleable-c2
tools.desc: TrustedSec's Malleable C2 profile and kit repo with sleep-jitter variants, AMSI/ETW patch examples, and profiles modeled on common user-agent traffic.
tools.when: Pick measurement-ready profiles with documented jitter/sleep tunables for detection lab comparisons.

tools.name: BC-SECURITY Malleable-C2-Profiles
tools.desc: Andy Hsu's curated profile set with editor/validator support and packaging guidance — a maintained alternative to the older collections.
tools.when: Structured, commented profiles for education and easy diffing against base beacon defaults.

tools.name: dnscat2
tools.desc: iagox86's DNS command-and-control tunnel: data rides inside DNS queries/responses (TXT/NS/CNAME/MX), by default plaintext unless you enable its built-in encryption.
tools.when: Proving DNS-based C2 in a lab where only DNS egress is allowed; watch the channel via passive-DNS correlation.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/iagox86/dnscat2.git && cd dnscat2/server && sudo gem install bundler && bundle install

tools.name: msfvenom
tools.desc: The payload generator inside Metasploit: raw, shellcode, and staged/stageless payloads for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and web platforms, with encoders and format outputs for every delivery stage.
tools.when: Authorized tests needing a payload in exactly the format your C2 staging (or a loader like Donut/ScareCrow) expects.
tools.install: apt install metasploit-framework  # then: msfvenom --list payloads

tools.name: Donut
tools.desc: Generates position-independent shellcode that stages .NET assemblies, PE files, and VBS/JScript entirely in memory, so a lab agent can be delivered without touching disk on the test host.
tools.when: Producing an in-memory delivery stage for a lab agent and observing how loaders that patch AMSI/ETW look from a defender's perspective.

tools.name: ScareCrow
tools.desc: Tylous's loader builder that wraps position-independent shellcode in benign-trusted formats (MSI, XLL, DLL sideload/renamed, HTA) using signed JScript/JS patterns for lab delivery testing.
tools.when: Lab research on how standard loaders hold up against modern EDR signatures — generate a loader and see what telemetry it leaves behind.

tools.name: CrossC2
tools.desc: Extension that generates cross-platform beacons for Cobalt Strike (Linux, macOS, Android/ARM, even ESXi) from a configured HTTPS listener, via genCrossC2 plus automatic Malleable C2 profile handling.
tools.when: Extending a Cobalt Strike lab to authorized non-Windows assets where stock Beacon cannot run, or studying cross-platform beacon metadata.
tools.install: Download genCrossC2 + CrossC2.cna from the GitHub release

tools.name: SILENTTRINITY
tools.desc: byt3bl33d3r's cross-platform post-exploitation C2 shell with a Python audit kit whose agents stage C# assemblies entirely in memory over HTTP — a reference for IronPython/C# and memory-only agent design.
tools.when: Studying memory-only C# stager architecture and the older 'Tasking the CLR' implant generation model in a lab.

tools.name: COFFLoader
tools.desc: TrustedSec's COFF (Common Object File Format)-in-memory loader that converts Cobalt Strike BOF object files into self-contained Windows executables and libraries, so BOFs run standalone.
tools.when: Run a library of lab BOFs (situational awareness, etc.) standalone, or turn BOFs into binaries that other tooling can invoke.

tools.name: CS-Situational-Awareness-BOF
tools.desc: TrustedSec's collection of Cobalt Strike BOFs for host situational awareness (enumeration, tokens, events) that doubles as a documented corpus of BOF/COFF development patterns.
tools.when: Lab practice: run battle-tested BOFs via COFFLoader or your C2 and study what beacon/BOF behavior defenders watch for.

tools.name: Ligolo-ng
tools.desc: Tunneling/pivoting tool that exposes a TUN interface and routes TCP/UDP through an agent over reverse TCP/TLS, reaching remote lab subnets without SOCKS/proxychains, with a web UI and autoroute since v0.8.
tools.when: Reaching the rest of an authorized test network from a C2 foothold — pivot activity blue teams should recognize and alert on.
tools.install: Download proxy & agent binaries from GitHub releases

tools.name: Chisel
tools.desc: Single-binary fast TCP/UDP tunnel carried over HTTP(S)/WebSocket (SSH-secured) with reverse port-forwarding and SOCKS — communication that reads as ordinary WebSocket/web traffic to defenders.
tools.when: Bridging egress-filtered lab segments to your C2, or tunnelling any service where the traffic should blend with normal HTTPS.

tools.name: cdncheck
tools.desc: ProjectDiscovery's CLI (with Go library and nuclei integration) that tags an IP/host as CDN, cloud, or WAF and can surface the true origin, mapping whether your C2 listeners sit behind hosted edge layers.
tools.when: Before fronting a C2 listener: know whether there's already a CDN/WAF in front of a host and whether the origin leaks elsewhere.

tools.name: cloudflared
tools.desc: Cloudflare Tunnel client: exposes a local listener through Cloudflare's edge (e.g. quick tunnels) so inbound C2/redirector traffic arrives via a CDN hop rather than your bare IP.
tools.when: Putting a lab C2 behind a legitimate edge service and validating that middlebox-only checks still detect your channel.

tools.name: gost
tools.desc: GO Simple Tunnel: multi-hop proxy chains (SOCKS5/HTTP/SSH/relay) with port forwarding, load balancing, and protocol obfuscation — a scriptable chaining engine for C2 redirector piping.
tools.when: Chain multiple redirectors/proxies on an authorized lab path and get per-hop logs while tuning traffic shapes.

tools.name: Stowaway
tools.desc: ph4ntonn's anti-detection multi-hop proxy for C2: agent mesh nodes support Socks5 and SSH forwarding with each hop adding a layer of encryption.
tools.when: Multi-hop proxy meshes in lab engagements where you want per-node encryption layers instead of plain port-forwarding.

tools.name: C2 Matrix
tools.desc: The community-maintained comparison of C2 frameworks: features, capabilities, listeners, transports, BOF support, and reporting across close to 100 frameworks, with a lab harness and Slingshot VM for testing them.
tools.when: Pick a C2 or compare implementation kits: one table to evaluate listeners, transports, and reporting before you install anything.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The authoritative knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques — read the C2-relevant techniques (T1071 Application Layer Protocol, T1573 Encrypted Channel) and the data sources defenders link back to them.
tools.when: Map which techniques your framework exercises and check the data sources you'll need to capture while testing.

tools.name: DetectionLab
tools.desc: Chris Long's Packer/Vagrant suite that builds a Windows domain pre-loaded with Sysmon, WEF, osquery, and Splunk plus hardened logging defaults (no longer actively maintained since 2023, but still widely used).
tools.when: Stand up an instrumented AD lab to show blue teams exactly what your C2 traffic emits across endpoints and network.
